testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: An air compressor governor stops the compressor from pumping air when the air tanks reach:
questions.explanation: An air compressor governor stops the compressor from pumping air when the air tanks reach 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: On a leaf spring, the leaves:
questions.explanation: When inspecting a vehicle's suspension, check for broken or missing leaves in leaf springs. This is dangerous. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing from any leaf spring, the vehicle cannot be driven.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: When it is hard for others to see your vehicle, such as at dawn or dusk, you can help other drivers by:

options.text: Waving an arm out the window.

questions.explanation: When visibility is low, turn your headlights to the low beam setting. If you cannot see others, they probably cannot see you either.

questions.question: Eating while driving is:

options.text: A good way to save time.
Acceptable if you are eating foods that are easy to eat.

questions.explanation: Smoking, eating, or drinking while driving are distracting activities and should be avoided. Plan ahead and stop to eat during long trips.

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side when you use them, it is a sign that:

options.text: The brakes need to be checked.
The brakes have too much stopping power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes need to be checked.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when braking, there may be a brake problem. Fix any brake issues before driving. Driving an unsafe vehicle breaks federal and state laws.

questions.question: When traveling in heavy traffic, the safest driving speed is:

options.text: A speed much slower than the flow of surrounding traffic.

questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, match the speed of surrounding vehicles. Vehicles traveling in the same direction at the same speed are less likely to collide. However, do not exceed legal speed limits.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road through it, so it may just look wet. Be very careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes is ____ in one minute.
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a single vehicle with air brakes, air should leak no more than 2 psi in one minute. Faster leaking means something needs repair and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: Before going downhill, you should:

options.text: Take your vehicle out of gear.
Rely only on braking to reduce your speed.

questions.explanation: On a steep downhill, use the engine's braking effect as your main way to control speed. Slow down and shift to a lower gear before starting the descent. Relying only on brakes can cause them to overheat and lose stopping power.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo:

options.text: Creates a low center of gravity.

questions.explanation: Hanging meat creates an unstable load. The truck may become top-heavy and swinging meat can affect steering. Drivers should be extra careful on sharp curves and highway ramps.

questions.question: When double clutching, if you stay in neutral too long and can't shift to the next gear, you should:

options.text: Stop the vehicle and start over.
Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up, and try again.
Skip your intended gear and move to the next one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up, and try again.
questions.explanation: If you stay in neutral too long and can't shift, don't force it. Return to neutral, release the clutch, increase engine speed to match road speed, and try again.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, you should:

options.text: Check the load and securing devices within the first 50 miles.
Not use your mirrors to look behind your vehicle.
Hold a cell phone in case of emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the load and securing devices within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo and securing devices before starting. During the trip, check again within the first 50 miles, every three hours or every 150 miles, and after each break.

questions.question: If a vehicle is over-length during a pre-trip inspection, the driver should:

options.text: Reduce the length of the load.
Make sure flags and lights for the oversize load are secure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure flags and lights for the oversize load are secure.
questions.explanation: If the load is oversize, confirm that all required signs, flags, lights, and reflectors are properly mounted. Also check that you have all required permits.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Only comes from physical distractions, not mental ones.
Can be made worse by pre-programming radio stations.
Can be avoided by eating while driving.
Can be avoided by not having complex conversations while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be avoided by not having complex conversations while driving.
questions.explanation: To reduce distraction, do not have complex or emotionally intense conversations while driving. Pre-program the radio before your trip and avoid eating, drinking, or smoking while driving. Mental distractions are as dangerous as physical ones.

questions.question: A header board is used to:

options.text: Help the driver see behind them.
Protect the driver from moving cargo.
Keep the driver from leaving the tractor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from moving cargo.
questions.explanation: A header board, also called a headache rack, protects the driver from cargo that shifts during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a crime that disqualifies someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: Several crimes disqualify a person from getting a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years. These include arson, robbery, and dishonesty crimes. More serious crimes like murder result in a lifetime ban.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
Controls how fast air leaves the storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air entering the storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air leaving the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: Failing to drain the tanks in an air brake system can result in:

options.text: Water freezing and causing brake failure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water freezing and causing brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks must be drained to remove water and oil. If water builds up and freezes in cold weather, it can cause brake failure.

questions.question: In cold weather, an alcohol evaporator should be checked and filled:
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice buildup in the air brake system. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: What happens if brake pads rub against brake drums and create too much heat?

options.text: The brakes will become extra sensitive.
The air compressor will kick on to cool the brakes.

questions.explanation: Brakes heat up when you use them. If they get too hot, they expand and change chemically. This makes them less effective and can cause them to stop working. This is called "brake fade."

questions.question: Where can you find the tire load rating?

options.text: On the inside of the driver's door
On the side of each tire

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of each tire
questions.explanation: The tire load rating is the maximum weight that a tire can safely carry at a certain pressure. This number is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: What can happen if your vehicle has a high center of gravity?

options.text: It may be difficult for you to see the road.
The tires may not be able to handle the weight.

questions.explanation: A vehicle's center of gravity is important for safety. A high center of gravity (such as cargo piled up high) makes your vehicle more likely to tip over.

questions.question: What is Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW)?

options.text: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
The total weight of a vehicle before cargo
The maximum weight allowed to be transported by a vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the combined total weight of a vehicle plus all of its cargo.

questions.question: When turning quickly to avoid an object in the road, you should:

options.text: Apply your brakes as you steer.
Give yourself extra clearance by turning more than needed to miss the object.
Turn just enough to miss the object and avoid turning more.
Steer and accelerate at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just enough to miss the object and avoid turning more.
questions.explanation: When turning quickly to avoid an object, turn only as much as you need to clear it. Do not brake while turning.

questions.question: How can you confirm that a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors connected to the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for the ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors connected to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires connected to the back of the brakes.

questions.question: When approaching a curve during the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Check traffic thoroughly in all directions.
Reduce your speed before entering the curve.
Keep your vehicle in its lane.
Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.
questions.explanation: When approaching a curve during the on-road driving test, check traffic in all directions. Reduce your speed enough before the curve so you don't need to brake or shift while in it. Keep your vehicle in its lane and keep checking traffic.

questions.question: What happens to shaded areas of the road?

options.text: They usually do not contain moisture, so they can't freeze.
They will stay slick after ice on other areas melts.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will stay slick after ice on other areas melts.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and stay cooler longer than other areas. Because they don't get direct sun, shady areas can stay icy and slippery even after ice melts from other parts of the road.

questions.question: If you are pulled off to the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Let your taillights alert other drivers.
Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
Keep your lights off to avoid distracting other drivers.
Keep your door open to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers. This is especially important at night. Taillights alone are not enough because other drivers might think you are moving normally and could hit you.

questions.question: On trucks and buses, where are ABS malfunction lamps located?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle by the passenger's door

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow malfunction lamps on the instrument panel. Trailers have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, either at the front or rear corner.

questions.question: During the pre-trip vehicle inspection test, which statement is true?

options.text: You do not need to identify the ABS.
You do not need to check windshield wipers.
You only need to check shock absorbers on one axle.
You should check the steering box for leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should check the steering box for leaks.
questions.explanation: During the external inspection, you must check that the steering box is mounted securely and is not leaking.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection skills test, you must:

options.text: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
Let the examiner check the vehicle.
Talk to a mechanic to show your knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: You must explain to the examiner what parts you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: When checking tire condition during the vehicle inspection, what should you look for?

options.text: The inside of the tires should be more worn than the outside.
The outside of the tires should be more worn than the inside.
The middle of the tires should be more worn than the outside.
The tires should have even wear across the entire tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires should have even wear across the entire tread.
questions.explanation: Tire treads should be worn evenly across the entire surface.

questions.question: Why should you use your mirrors to look at your tires frequently?

options.text: To see if the tires are rolling properly.
To check if the tread is deep enough.
To compare the size of the tires to other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Check your tires regularly in your mirrors to notice a tire fire if one starts. Tire fires can happen when tires are under-inflated, when dual tires touch each other, or when tires overheat.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:
questions.explanation: For a normal stop in a vehicle with air brakes, press the brake pedal down. The harder you press, the more air pressure releases.

questions.question: After starting the vehicle during the pre-trip inspection, what should the coolant temperature do?
questions.explanation: Watch the gauges after starting your vehicle. The coolant temperature should gradually rise to the normal operating range.

questions.question: The brake pedal is part of which brake system?
questions.explanation: The service brake system applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
They can replace flat mirrors completely.
They help you see a wider area.
They are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help you see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles have curved, convex mirrors. They let you see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, they also make objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Prevent the wheels from locking up
Stop a vehicle from speeding uphill
Stop a vehicle from speeding downhill

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents the wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: What does poor weight balance do?

options.text: Makes the vehicle harder to handle.
Makes the vehicle easier to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes the vehicle harder to handle.
questions.explanation: When a load is poorly balanced, it makes the vehicle difficult and unsafe to handle.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop shortly to:

options.text: Check that the wheel nuts are tight.
Check that the tire has enough air pressure.
Confirm the correct tire was changed.
Make sure no other tires were damaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the wheel nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop after a short distance and check that the wheel nuts are tight.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you will be checked on traffic awareness. You should NOT:

options.text: Look for pedestrians on the road.

questions.explanation: During the driving test, check traffic regularly and use your mirrors often, especially at intersections. Watch for pedestrians in areas where they may be.

questions.question: The service brake system:

options.text: Controls the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Controls the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three separate parts: the service brake, the parking brake, and the emergency brake. The service brake system controls the brakes when you use the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: If your vehicle's ABS stops working while driving, you should:

options.text: Use the parking brake to stop.

questions.explanation: If ABS stops working, your regular brakes still work. Drive and brake normally.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Try to get out of their way.

questions.explanation: If facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way, avoid making eye contact, and ignore their gestures. Do not respond or try to challenge them.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks usually:
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity and need careful driving. The cargo can shift during transport, which changes how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Take your foot off the brake pedal.
Turn quickly toward the direction of the skid.
Turn back after the vehicle straightens out.

questions.explanation: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, release the brake pedal so the wheels can roll again. Turn quickly toward the skid direction, then turn back to straighten the vehicle.

questions.question: When carrying 30 feet of cargo on a flatbed trailer, use at least ____ tie-downs.
questions.explanation: Use one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Any cargo, no matter the size, needs at least two tie-downs.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you are about to brake?

options.text: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times.
Stick your arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap the brake pedal a few times to make your brake lights flash. This warns drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: When should you turn off your turn signal?
questions.explanation: Keep your turn signal on during the entire turn. Turn it off only after the turn is complete.
